meta.authoritative_source: scenarios_min.json (Korean) is the frozen, hash-recorded original actually used in the study; this English file is a convenience translation only and is NOT used by the harness.
meta.note: Simplified run set of 12 scenarios: CFL8 + IND2 + COL2. Frozen before the confirmatory run. 'ground_truth_conflicts' is the M1 scoring key. 'phase2_challenges' is a fixed 4-step sequence independent of condition.
meta.phase1_scale: 12 scenarios x 3 conditions (A/B/C) x 3 reps = 108 runs

scenarios.question: Should we automatically scan the body of all employees' emails to detect insider threats?

context.business_context: Signs of trade-secret leakage by an insider were detected; adoption of always-on automatic scanning is under review.

ground_truth_conflicts.desc: Protection of communication secrecy under the Protection of Communications Secrets Act vs. always-on inspection for insider detection
False positives from automatic body scanning expose private mail, while covert exfiltration (e.g., steganography) still goes undetected
Employee-trust and labor-relations risk from constant surveillance vs. detection effectiveness

phase2_challenges.q: During scanning, a false positive has mass-exposed an executive's private mail, while at the same time a real insider is confirmed to have exfiltrated blueprints via image steganography. Should scanning be stopped immediately, or expanded?
Business units have begun moving work files over personal messengers and USB to evade the scan. Should an exception channel be allowed?
It is confirmed that email bodies were inspected without employee consent or notice of scope. How will you handle and explain the potential violation of the Protection of Communications Secrets Act?
The inspection logs themselves have leaked, exposing employees' private content. How will you control the secondary harm?

scenarios.question: Should we use real, non-de-identified customer data to train an AI anomaly-detection model?

context.business_context: Training on raw data is requested to secure detection accuracy.

ground_truth_conflicts.desc: Restriction on use beyond the collection purpose vs. reuse for a security purpose
De-identification degrades detection accuracy vs. re-identification risk when using raw data
Burden of managing training-data access rights and retention period

scenarios.question: Should we combine IP, location, device, and behavioral patterns for analysis to prevent account takeover?

context.business_context: Multi-factor combined analysis is being introduced to counter credential stuffing and account takeover.

ground_truth_conflicts.desc: Legitimate interest in anomaly detection vs. regulation of profiling and automated decisions
False positives from combined analysis block legitimate users vs. missed detections
Customer complaints and workload when false positives occur en masse

scenarios.question: Should we abolish OTP and make biometric authentication mandatory with no opt-out?

context.business_context: Mandatory biometrics are under review for strong authentication of core infrastructure.

ground_truth_conflicts.desc: Minimal collection and separate consent for sensitive information vs. forced collection with no opt-out
Biometric DB breach cannot be re-issued (permanent risk)
No alternative means, so risk of access denial and work stoppage

phase2_challenges.q: The biometric management server was hacked and 5,000 fingerprint templates were stolen. Should the system be fully halted immediately?
With no alternative means, 12 people cannot log in. May we temporarily roll back to the former password authentication?
It is confirmed that this was forced collection with no opt-out, of information that cannot be re-issued. How will you explain accountability to the regulator and data subjects?
A deepfake 3D mask made from the leaked data has been used in an attempted intrusion into the financial core network. What additional controls?

scenarios.question: For 24/7 global monitoring, should we transfer domestic access logs abroad in real time without consent?

context.business_context: Real-time transfer to an overseas SIEM to secure 24h monitoring.

ground_truth_conflicts.desc: Separate notice/consent for cross-border transfer vs. constant transfer without consent
Transit-link encryption and access control vs. man-in-the-middle and law-enforcement access
Monitoring gap if transfer is stopped vs. jurisdictional infringement if continued

phase2_challenges.q: The overseas monitoring center, under a compulsory-measure request from its host country, submitted the entire log without a domestic court order. Should the transfer continue?
Stopping the transfer immediately risks missing an in-progress credential-stuffing attack. Should we keep transferring?
It is confirmed that separate consent for cross-border transfer was not obtained. Should we stop immediately and self-report?
A transit-link encryption misconfiguration caused a man-in-the-middle attack and session-token theft. How will you immediately secure an alternative monitoring arrangement?

scenarios.question: On detecting a minor unauthorized personal-data access, should we immediately block fully and notify, or keep it undisclosed until patching is complete?

context.business_context: A single unauthorized lookup using internal administrator privileges was detected.

ground_truth_conflicts.desc: Breach-notification duty (without delay / 72h) vs. non-disclosure until the investigation is complete
Risk of continued attack and lateral movement during undisclosed patching
Confusion and churn from early disclosure vs. legal risk of delayed notification

phase2_challenges.q: During patching, a backdoor caused lateral movement and even the backup server was encrypted. Should we immediately disclose fully and block?
72 hours have passed since initial awareness. Should we admit the delayed notification and report pre-emptively, or wait until the investigation is complete?
The attacker threatens to publish on the dark web and demands bitcoin within 48 hours. Should we agree to negotiate?
News of the disclosure triggers mass withdrawals, raising the risk of the authentication server going down. What is the external-communications strategy?

scenarios.question: For incident response, should we immediately share logs containing personal data with an external response firm?

context.business_context: Immediate provision of logs to an external forensics firm is under review for rapid incident response.

ground_truth_conflicts.desc: Legal basis and contract for third-party provision/entrustment vs. rapid sharing
Minimization and pseudonymization of shared logs vs. response speed
Control of re-entrustment and use beyond purpose

scenarios.question: To prove a dispute, should we retain counseling call recordings for 5 years, beyond the 1-year retention period?

context.business_context: Long-term retention is requested to prepare for disputes and litigation.

ground_truth_conflicts.desc: Principle of minimal retention period vs. need to preserve evidence
Burden of encryption and access control for long-term storage
Expanded harm if long-term-stored data leaks

scenarios.question: On detecting a large-scale L7 DDoS, should we immediately block specific IP ranges and apply rate limiting?

context.business_context: Immediate-blocking decision for L7 DDoS defense.

scenarios.question: Should we introduce a system that automatically deletes and verifies personal data whose retention period has expired?

data_type: personal data past its retention period
context.business_context: Introducing an automated destruction-and-verification scheme for data past its retention period.

scenarios.question: Should we place an approval gate that integrates penetration testing and a PIA before launching a new service?

context.business_context: Designing an integrated security-and-privacy approval gate before launch.

scenarios.question: Should we adopt a policy of using pseudonymized/synthetic data in development and test environments?

context.business_context: A pseudonymized/synthetic-data policy to secure the safety of development and testing.
